title: 2-week Node.js skill test plan
summary: Prepare for a timed Node.js skill test: 16 lessons, 23 runnable TypeScript exercises checked in the browser, a Node.js flashcard deck and two runs of the timed simulator. About 1–1.5 hours a day.

rhythm.text: Read one or two lessons, try every gotcha before opening its answer, then make the exercises pass without looking at the hints first.
Timed practice or a full test, then review: reread the lessons for weak topics and clear due flashcards.

rules: Predict the order of logs before you run event loop code.
Never block the event loop in a request path: no sync I/O and no long CPU loops.
Every promise is awaited or has a catch, and every emitter or stream has an error listener.
Treat all input as untrusted: validate it, parameterise queries and never build shell strings.
Keep the timer honest in practice runs: no notes and no pausing.

typescript: Type async functions by their resolved value: async function load(): Promise<User>.
Catch errors as unknown and narrow with instanceof Error before reading message.
Model results that can fail as a discriminated union: { ok: true, value } | { ok: false, error }.
Use generics for reusable helpers such as caches and pools: class LruCache<K, V>.
Mark config objects readonly once validated so the rest of the app cannot change them.

phases.title: Runtime and async Node.js
phases.check: Without notes, predict the output of mixed timer, promise and nextTick code, and write a concurrency-limited task runner with error handling.

phases.title: Servers in production and the test
phases.check: Score 70% or more in every topic of the timed simulator, and pass both coding tasks within the time limit.

weeks.title: Runtime, async code, errors, events and streams
weeks.focus: How the event loop orders work, CommonJS and ES modules, promises and concurrency limits, error handling, EventEmitter, streams and bytes. Finish with a timed practice run.

tip.typescript: Type callbacks and promise results explicitly, and use unknown for caught errors until you narrow them.

weeks.title: HTTP APIs, operations, performance, security and tooling
weeks.focus: Middleware and routing, REST conventions, config and graceful shutdown, scaling across cores, caching, common attacks, testing with fake timers and npm versions. Finish with the full timed test.

tip.typescript: Model request handlers and middleware with small types, and validate untrusted input before you narrow it to a typed object.
